newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas rises in West due to outage.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas rises in West due to outage.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were higher again in the West due to the plant outage in British Columbia and continuing maintenance in Alberta, traders said.
Westcoast Energy's 750 million cubic feet a day Fort Nelson gas plant in northeastern B.C., was not expected to complete a maintenance outage until June 18.

Spot prices at Sumas, Wash., rose another five cents to about $1.29-1.31 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), traders said, noting sporadic constraints in the Rockies also kept supply tight in the Northwest.
Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was quoted at C$1.56/1.57 per gigajoule, up one cent from Wednesday.
July AECO was talked at C$1.52, while July/October AECO remained at C$1.515/1.53.
Tempering demand in Alberta was the drop in storage injections to about 700 mmcfd, one Calgary-based trader said, down from about 750 mmcfd earlier in the week.
In eastern Canada, prices at Niagara slipped two cents to about $2.29-2.31 per mmBtu.
